blocks.text: In organic chemistry, the structural unit >C=O is known as carbonyl group. Aldehydes and ketones are the classes of compounds that contain a carbonyl group. The general structures of aldehydes and ketones are given below.

blocks.alt: General structures: R-C(=O)-H labelled Aldehydes and R-C(=O)-R labelled Ketones, each with the O drawn above the carbonyl carbon.
blocks.caption: General structures of aldehydes and ketones (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 102).

blocks.text: These compounds are abundant in nature and their large quantities are synthesised every year. Aldehydes are present in many spices, fruits, and natural fragrances. Ketones used in pharmaceuticals, chemicals, and paint industries. The most common ketone is acetone, which is found in nail polish removers.

blocks.title: Interesting Information
blocks.text:
The smell and taste of bitter almond is due to benzaldehyde, which is produced due to the oxidation of terpenes.
Acetone (propanone) are used in nail polish removers.
book_errors: produced due to the oxidation of terpenes

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book says that the benzaldehyde of bitter almond is produced by the oxidation of terpenes. In bitter almonds benzaldehyde is set free when amygdalin, a compound in the seed, is hydrolysed; it does not come from terpenes.

blocks.alt: Benzaldehyde: a benzene ring carrying a CHO group, C double-bonded to O with H below. Acetone (propanone): a C double-bonded to O above it, with H3C and CH3 below, labelled 'Acetone (Propanone)'.
blocks.caption: Benzaldehyde and acetone (propanone), from the Interesting Information box (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 102).
